summary: Keeps a main and a backup key for each paid service and switches to the backup when the main key runs out or is rejected.
purpose: Keeps AI and search calls working when the first key is spent, and avoids paying for a failing request again and again.
why: The header says that a spent or rejected main key is parked for a cool-down so that every request does not repeat the failed round trip.
how: Each service has an ordered list of key names, main first and backup second. The parts that were not included in this packet are supposed to track which keys are spent or parked and pick the next usable one, but their code is not visible here.
inputs: The names of the key settings in the environment and the provider name.
outputs: The key slots for each provider, and status information that does not include any key value.
risks: The code described in the header is not fully visible, so the exact switching rules cannot be confirmed from this packet.
debug: Start by checking which key names are set in the environment for the failing service. Then check the status report to see whether the main key is parked. Reset the chain if a key was fixed but is still parked.
